likelihood_status: draft estimates, all to be curated by the owner

threats.name: Death
threats.description: The person dies; their ability to act is gone and what they only know in their head is lost.

threats.name: Incapacity
threats.description: Illness, dementia, coma or injury; the person cannot act or recall, possibly only for a while.

threats.name: Impaired judgement
threats.description: The person is drunk, high or otherwise not in their right mind. They may say or show things they would not, hand over access, or act on what they can reach or know (move funds, send a transaction, wipe or destroy things).

threats.name: Amnesia
threats.description: The person forgets what they only know in their head (PIN, passphrase, where something is).

threats.name: Turns malicious or disloyal
threats.description: A trusted person turns against the others (greed, feud, separation) and uses what they can reach or know.

threats.name: Sabotage
threats.description: A trusted person destroys or hides what they can reach, out of spite or to block others.

threats.name: Collusion
threats.description: Several people conspire and combine what each of them can reach or know.

threats.name: Coercion
threats.description: A person is forced by threats or violence (wrench attack, extortion, kidnapping) to hand over access or knowledge.

threats.name: Social engineering
threats.description: A person is tricked into revealing what they know or into granting access (fake support, impersonation, phishing).

threats.name: Reveals holdings
threats.description: A person talks about the holdings or the setup; the knowledge that funds exist makes the people and places a target.

threats.name: Unreachable
threats.description: The person cannot be found or contacted when needed (moved abroad, estranged, travelling, imprisoned).

threats.name: Fire
threats.description: Fire destroys what is stored at the location.

likelihood_modifiers.reason: Fire rarely reaches vaults or underground places.

threats.name: Water
threats.description: Flood, burst pipe, rain or groundwater destroys what is stored at the location.

likelihood_modifiers.reason: Bank vaults are protected against water.
Groundwater and damp reach buried and walled-in places.

threats.name: Natural disaster
threats.description: Earthquake, storm, landslide or tsunami hits the whole area and crushes or buries what is stored in it.

likelihood.ask: Which natural hazards (earthquake, flood, storm) are common in the area of the locations?

threats.name: Environmental degradation
threats.description: Long-term damp, heat, corrosion or pests slowly damage what is stored at the location.

threats.name: Forceful attack, local
threats.description: Criminals, burglars or an authority raid break in and take or read what they find; limited to this location.

likelihood_modifiers.reason: Known to many people and weakly protected.

threats.name: Forceful attack, area-wide
threats.description: War, bombing, mass riot or a siege hits the whole area; every location close enough is affected.

likelihood.ask: Is the region exposed to war, riots or sieges?

threats.name: Unauthorised access
threats.description: Someone who is not on the access list gets in (visitor, cleaner, tradesperson, family member, staff) and can see or take what is stored.

likelihood_modifiers.reason: Access is controlled or the place is secret.
Locked or hidden inside the home.

threats.name: Accidental discovery
threats.description: Construction work, digging, renovation, animals or treasure hunters uncover a hidden location.

threats.name: Jurisdictional change
threats.description: Laws, borders or regimes change: confiscation, capital controls, mandatory disclosure, ban on self-custody, forced access.

likelihood.ask: How stable is the legal regime of the jurisdiction (confiscation, capital controls, forced access)?

threats.name: Temporarily inaccessible
threats.description: The location cannot be reached when needed (travel ban, war, pandemic, closed opening hours, distance, blocked road).

threats.name: Lost
threats.description: The exact place is forgotten or no longer exists (spot cannot be found, built over, demolished).

likelihood_modifiers.reason: Hard to find again after many years.

threats.name: Control lost
threats.description: The property is sold, the relative moves away or dies, the lease ends or the box is closed for unpaid fees.

threats.name: Box frozen, seized or opened
threats.description: The bank or an authority freezes, drills or empties the safe deposit box (court order, insolvency, lien, unpaid fees).

likelihood.ask: How likely are freezes or seizures of safe deposit boxes in the jurisdiction?

threats.name: Provider staff access
threats.description: Staff of the bank or cloud provider look at or take the contents.

threats.name: Cloud account lost
threats.description: The account is suspended, deleted, locked or its credentials are lost, or the provider shuts down.

threats.name: Cloud breach or account takeover
threats.description: The provider is breached or the account is taken over; files are copied.

threats.name: Opened without trace
threats.description: A skilled attacker opens and reseals the bag (heat, cold, solvents) without visible signs.

threats.name: Swapped
threats.description: The bag is replaced by a look-alike (forged or copied serial, or the serial is never compared) and the contents are replaced or copied.

threats.name: Seal fails
threats.description: The adhesive ages or reacts to heat and cold, so the bag opens or looks tampered by itself; the seal signal becomes unreliable.

threats.name: Lost or illegible
threats.description: The strip is lost or its serial is unreadable; the bag can no longer be verified.

threats.name: Swapped together with the bag
threats.description: An attacker who reaches both the bag and its strip replaces both, so the comparison still matches.

threats.name: Incorrect serial
threats.description: The serial was copied wrongly, so a genuine bag looks forged or a forged bag looks genuine.

threats.name: Backdoor
threats.description: The vendor or a state has built in a weakness, a leak or a remote switch.

threats.name: Leaks seed or key
threats.description: A flaw leaks key material (implementation bug, side channel, nonce reuse); every device of the same model is affected.

threats.name: Key leaks through signature nonces
threats.description: A malicious or compromised device hides key bits in the nonces of its signatures; over several signatures the key is recoverable.

threats.name: Malware on an online device
threats.description: Malicious software runs on an internet-connected phone or computer: it reads the seeds and files kept there and manipulates what the coordinator on it shows and sends.

threats.name: Breaks
threats.description: Hardware failure, drop or water damage, or the storage dies; the device is dead and everything kept only on it is gone.

threats.name: Ageing
threats.description: After years of storage the flash memory, battery or connectors no longer work.

threats.name: Supply-chain attack
threats.description: The device is modified on its way to the owner (hardware implant, preinstalled firmware, preset seed).

likelihood_modifiers.reason: Resellers and mail hops are outside the vendor's control.

threats.name: Malicious firmware
threats.description: Downloaded or provided firmware is malicious (fake site, unsigned file, compromised update channel).

threats.name: Firmware bug
threats.description: A non-malicious defect makes the device derive wrong addresses, sign wrongly or lose its seed.

threats.name: Update bricks the device
threats.description: A firmware update fails or is interrupted and the device no longer starts.

threats.name: PIN brute-forced
threats.description: An attacker with the device tries PINs without being stopped by a wipe or a growing delay.

threats.name: Wiped by wrong PIN attempts
threats.description: Too many wrong PIN attempts (owner, child, attacker) wipe the device and the seed on it.

threats.name: Seed extracted from the chip
threats.description: With the device in hand and enough effort (glitching, probing, memory dump) the seed is read out despite the PIN.

threats.name: Swapped
threats.description: An attacker swaps the device for a prepared look-alike; the owner later enters the PIN or loads the seed into the fake.

threats.name: Lost or stolen
threats.description: The device is lost or stolen, often while it is carried; whatever is not protected on it is exposed.

likelihood_modifiers.reason: Phones and laptops are carried around and easily lost or stolen.

threats.name: Attack through the connection
threats.description: A compromised computer or phone attacks or manipulates the device over USB, Bluetooth or NFC.

threats.name: Signs blind
threats.description: The device cannot check outputs, change or the multisig policy (descriptor not registered, small screen), so a malicious coordinator can redirect funds.

threats.name: Shows one thing, signs another
threats.description: The device displays a receiver, amount or change that differs from what it actually signs.

threats.name: No power when needed
threats.description: The battery is dead or expired (AAA cells, internal battery) or no suitable power source is at hand.

threats.name: Obsolete interface
threats.description: The connector, card slot, wireless stack or companion app of the device is no longer available or supported on current hardware.

threats.name: Discontinued
threats.description: The vendor goes out of business or stops support: no updates, no companion app, no replacement.

threats.name: Too little entropy
threats.description: The seed, passphrase or password was generated with too little randomness (weak RNG, too few dice rolls, biased dice, short or guessable choice) and can be guessed.

threats.name: Manipulated random number generator
threats.description: The random number generator used to create the secret (device, phone, password manager, website) is deliberately weakened or predictable.

threats.name: Supplied by someone else
threats.description: The secret was handed over rather than made by the owner (seed card in the box, default PIN, example passphrase from a tutorial, generator website) and is already known to them.

threats.name: Observed while created
threats.description: Cameras (laptop, phone, room), microphones, radio sensing (Wi-Fi) or bystanders record or infer the secret while it is generated, written down or spoken.

threats.name: Observed while entered
threats.description: The secret is seen, filmed, heard (keystroke or button sounds) or captured by a compromised keyboard or host while it is typed or read out.

threats.name: Entered on an online device
threats.description: The secret is typed or scanned into an internet-connected computer or phone (restore, test, hot wallet, password field).

threats.name: Phished
threats.description: The secret is entered on a fake wallet, a fake recovery site or given to a fake support agent.

threats.name: Reused
threats.description: The same secret is used elsewhere (other wallet, other device, other account) and leaks through that other place.

threats.name: Forgotten
threats.description: The secret is forgotten or its last copy is lost.

threats.name: Entered differently
threats.description: Case, spaces, keyboard layout, Unicode normalisation, word list language or keypad layout differ between devices; a different, empty wallet opens or the unlock fails.

threats.name: Incorrect checksum
threats.description: A seed made by hand has an invalid last word and cannot be restored on devices that check it.

threats.name: Weakness in the seed scheme or key derivation
threats.description: A flaw in the word encoding, the mnemonic-to-seed hashing (PBKDF2, HMAC-SHA512) or the key derivation lets an attacker narrow down or derive the keys.

threats.name: Incorrect or outdated
threats.description: The saved descriptor has a typo, a wrong or old cosigner, a wrong derivation path, or predates a change of the wallet.

threats.name: Cannot be imported
threats.description: The format or version of the descriptor cannot be read by the coordinator or device that is available.

threats.name: Derivation unknown
threats.description: The script type or derivation path is forgotten, or the standard one is assumed although the wallet uses another; funds are not found.

threats.name: Incorrect policy
threats.description: Threshold, signer set or timelock were set up differently from what was planned (wrong cosigner, duplicate key, wrong threshold).

threats.name: Timelock not refreshed in time
threats.description: The coins are not moved before the delay of a recovery path expires; its signers can spend earlier than intended.

threats.name: Policy not supported by tools
threats.description: Coordinators or devices available later cannot handle the timelock or custom policy, so the recovery path cannot be used.

threats.name: Recovery transaction does not confirm
threats.description: Fee spikes or a congested mempool delay the recovery or sweep transaction.

threats.name: Holdings traced on chain
threats.description: Address reuse, chain analysis or links to exchanges reveal balances and the structure of the wallet.

threats.name: Weakness in the signature scheme
threats.description: A flaw or advance (quantum computing, biased nonces, a curve attack) lets an attacker forge signatures or derive private keys from public data.

likelihood.ask: How seriously should a break of the signature scheme (e.g. quantum computing) within 50 years be taken?

threats.name: Weakness in the hash functions
threats.description: A flaw in SHA-256, RIPEMD-160 or the script-hash construction lets an attacker find another script or key for the same address.

threats.name: Consensus or relay policy change
threats.description: A soft or hard fork or a relay policy change makes a script type, timelock or output size invalid, unspendable or uneconomic.

threats.name: Malicious send transaction
threats.description: The coordinator builds a transaction with the wrong receiver.

threats.name: Malicious receive address
threats.description: The coordinator shows an address that does not belong to the wallet when receiving.

threats.name: Malicious change address
threats.description: The coordinator sends the change of a transaction to a wrong address.

threats.name: Compromised host
threats.description: Malware on the computer or phone running the coordinator replaces addresses, reads xpubs or manipulates transactions.

threats.name: Backdoor
threats.description: The vendor or a state has built in a weakness, a leak or a remote switch.

threats.name: Malicious software
threats.description: Downloaded or provided software is malicious (fake website, unsigned or unverified binary, compromised repository or update channel).

threats.name: Software bug
threats.description: A non-malicious defect miscalculates fees or change, hides funds beyond the gap limit or mishandles multisig or timelocks.

threats.name: Backend learns the wallet
threats.description: The server or node the coordinator queries learns xpubs, addresses and balances.

threats.name: Discontinued
threats.description: The vendor or project stops maintaining or distributing the coordinator.

threats.name: Deleted
threats.description: The application or its wallet file is deleted or lost with the computer.

threats.name: Illegible
threats.description: The backup can no longer be read (smudged, scratched, corroded, faded, unclear handwriting).

threats.name: Ageing
threats.description: The medium degrades over the years (paper, bit rot and charge loss in flash media).

threats.name: Found
threats.description: Someone who was not meant to finds the backup and recognises what it is.

threats.name: Copied unnoticed
threats.description: Someone with short access photographs or copies the backup without leaving a trace.

threats.name: Incorrect
threats.description: The backup was wrong or incomplete from the start (transcription error, wrong order, missing word, wrong file).

threats.name: Lost
threats.description: The backup is misplaced, forgotten, thrown away or stolen as a thing of no value.

threats.name: Replaced or altered
threats.description: An attacker alters or replaces the backup (other words, an attacker's xpub in a descriptor) so that a later recovery or sweep goes to him.

threats.name: Read on a compromised computer
threats.description: A digital backup is opened on an infected computer and copied.

threats.name: Deleted or overwritten
threats.description: A digital backup is deleted, overwritten, formatted or encrypted by ransomware.

threats.name: Obsolete medium or format
threats.description: Readers or software for the medium or file format are no longer available.

threats.name: Cannot be decrypted
threats.description: An encrypted item cannot be decrypted although the key exists (tool or algorithm no longer available, corrupted file).

threats.name: Weakness in the encryption
threats.description: The cipher, key derivation or tool that encrypts an item is broken or too weak against offline brute force.

threats.name: Outdated
threats.description: The plan was not updated after changes or not reviewed in time; helpers follow wrong instructions.

threats.name: Lost or forgotten
threats.description: The plan or its copies are gone, or the heirs and trustees do not know that it exists or where it is.

threats.name: Not understood
threats.description: The plan is too technical, ambiguous or incomplete for the people who must follow it.
